text:
elaine_sales: Quick: enterprise payments prospect wants Private Deploy POC. Requirements: PrivateLink isolation, per-AZ HA, TGW/BGP as on-prem fallback, monthly EIP rotation for compliance, and they must correlate original client IP in Redwood auth logs. Need a concise netops handoff + security checklist and firewall snippet to paste into their ticket.

rob_neteng: Short answer: PrivateLink interface endpoints NAT to the ENI so original client IP is not visible server-side. Ways to preserve or correlate identity: (1) deploy an in-VPC egress proxy that inserts X-Forwarded-For or a custom header; (2) use PROXY protocol between their proxy and our edge so we receive the real TCP source IP (works best for TCP), or (3) route via TGW with a customer NAT EIP/BYOIP so logs show known EIP (requires customer static IPs). If they need cryptographic client identity use mTLS client certs.

mina_arch: Infra notes: create interface endpoints in each AZ and front them with a small autoscaling HA proxy group (active-active). Enable PrivateLink private DNS so the service FQDN resolves locally. For cross-region either replicate VPCEs or use an inter-region TGW. BGP failover pattern: prefer VPCE local routes and advertise TGW prefixes as lower-priority; we can share a sample route-preference config.

samir_security: Security checklist (paste-ready):
- Provide KMS key policy snapshot and audit-log retention requirement; confirm TLS mode (mTLS recommended) and cert rotation cadence.
- Agree monthly EIP rotation schedule and maintenance windows; provide automation for firewall updates or accept an FQDN-based allowlist with documented TTLs.

rob_neteng: Minimal firewall snippet for their ops (replace placeholders):
```
# egress from customer VPC -> Redwood POC
allow tcp from 10.1.0.0/16 to 52.14.200.99/32 port 443
# if using VPCE, allow to VPCE ENIs or VPCE ID
allow tcp from 10.1.0.0/16 to vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f 443
# healthchecks from our probe pool
allow tcp from 10.1.0.0/16 <- 15.90.10.0/24 443
```
Note: if customer inspects TLS and rewrites SNI, prefer mTLS or PROXY protocol to avoid certificate mismatches.

mina_arch: Cost note for sales: PrivateLink has per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing charges. Peering/TGW removes per-endpoint fees but may have transit costs and more ops. For a short POC (<1TB/mo) PrivateLink is simplest; for sustained multi-TB egress, recommend TGW/peering or Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. Share expected egress GB and peak RPS and well produce numbers.

elaine_sales: Can someone paste a 3-line netops handoff I can drop into the ticket and a 2-line security checklist? They want kickoff in 7 business days.

rob_neteng: 3-line netops handoff: 
- Provision PrivateLink interface endpoints in each AZ and front them with HA proxies; enable PrivateLink DNS for service resolution.
- PrivateLink NATs client IP; to preserve original src IP either run an in-VPC egress proxy that inserts X-Forwarded-For or use PROXY protocol, or route via TGW with a customer NAT EIP if a static IP is available.
- Open outbound TCP/443 to assigned EIP(s) or VPCE IDs; monthly EIP rotation requires a maintenance window and automation to update firewall rules. Expect per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing charges.

samir_security: Blockers before POC: their network diagram, expected monthly egress (GB), peak RPS, confirmation on TLS inspection (SNI rewrite), and EIP rotation automation.

ticket_bot: ticket-bot: Created ticket POC-99901-net-handoff and assigned to #eng-infra; ETA: 3 business days.

elaine_sales: I'll upload their network diagram and traffic estimates to POC-99901. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
